It installs restricted-VIP DNS + routing for *.googleapis.com — and removes the tenant's default internet route. Cloud Run is *.run.app, which is neither.
VPC Peering provisioning model. Observed live, greenfield, 2026-09-04 — docs/repro/dns-peering.md

div.div: Enabling VPC-SC did not make the peered DNS domain unnecessary — it is what made it necessary.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 727px; margin-left: 761px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #174EA6;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#174EA6, #84b3ff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Before enablement the tenant reached Cloud Run over its own default internet route. Enablement removes that route and installs a replacement for *.googleapis.com only.
The claim's mechanism is real and is doing exactly what was described — in Lane A. Lane B is not a googleapis.com name, so nothing in that redirect covers it. The causality is inverted.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 815px; margin-left: 761px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #5F6368;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#5F6368, #96999d); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
The restricted-VIP static route and its custom-route export were also tested (added at a fourth state): no change, 200 either side. The peered DNS domain alone is load-bearing.
Not shown: pointing the run.app zone at the PRIVATE VIP (199.36.153.8/30) produces the identical 503 while your VMs keep returning 200 — see docs/repro/dns-peering.md §6.2.
